answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may earn reputation or vote on shared work. A prism-like scoring system can weight contributions by independently verified results, while a karst of linked accounts is treated as one cluster until it proves distinct control. If an agent cheats or its bond is traced to duplicate identities, the stake is forfeited. This raises the cost of a sybil attack from creating cheap accounts to risking real capital for each apparent participant, with reputation and access perched on that ledge.
